plans.note: Section 7 is captioned 'Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor' and is the controlling location. Check whether the cap is mutual or one-way in Contractor's favour, whether a dollar/fees-based figure is stated, and whether carve-outs (IP infringement, confidentiality, gross negligence/wilful misconduct, indemnity obligations) are preserved. The heading pairing liability limits with an indemnity running to Contractor suggests a vendor-favourable drafting posture.

Section 7 expressly contains an indemnity in favour of Contractor, i.e. running the wrong direction. Confirm whether any Contractor-to-Clear Capital indemnity (third-party IP infringement, negligence/wilful misconduct, breach of confidentiality) exists there or is tucked into the Section 5 warranty block; if none, treat the vendor-side indemnity as missing and the customer-side indemnity as overbroad.

No covenants/restrictive-covenant section appears in the outline. Any restriction on Clear Capital's business or sourcing would most plausibly sit in Section 1 (Purpose of Engagement) as a scope-of-engagement limitation; scan there and in the unnumbered Section 2 gap before concluding absence.

No exclusivity heading exists. Check Section 1 for language making Contractor the sole or exclusive provider of the Services and Section 3 for compensation terms conditioned on exclusive engagement. Note the outline skips Section 2, so confirm against the full text.

Pricing terms live in Section 3 (Contractor's Compensation); an MFN, if present, would be a most-favoured-pricing or best-rates covenant there. Rule is directional — only flag if it obliges Clear Capital to give RadialSpark our best terms; an MFN in our favour is welcome.

No personnel or restrictive-covenant section is listed. Consultant-style agreements often place a no-hire of Contractor's staff near the engagement scope (Section 1) or the survival language in Section 6; check both for duration and a general-advertising carve-out before marking missing.

Section 6 (Termination) is the primary location. Verify Clear Capital has convenience termination on reasonable notice with no penalty or acceleration of unearned fees, and check whether Contractor holds a symmetric convenience right to walk mid-engagement, which we resist.

No term/renewal heading appears; the term may sit in the unlisted Section 2 or in Section 6. Consulting engagements of this type are often fixed-scope with no auto-renewal. Check Section 6 for evergreen extension language and any non-renewal notice window or price-uplift mechanic.

The outline shows no general/miscellaneous provisions section, which is where governing law and venue normally sit. Check the tail of Section 7 and the end of the document for a trailing boilerplate block; New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales with courts (not foreign arbitration) is acceptable.

No miscellaneous section is listed. Assignment and change-of-control language, if present, may appear near termination in Section 6 or in unnumbered closing text. Confirm we may assign to affiliates and successors and that RadialSpark cannot terminate on our change of control.

Section 4 (Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance) governs. Confirm deliverables and any materials we pay for vest in Clear Capital (work-for-hire plus present assignment), that our pre-existing IP and data are not assigned to Contractor, and that acceptance criteria tie back to the Specifications.

Any licence-back of Contractor background or retained materials will sit in Section 4 alongside ownership. Check the grant is perpetual/irrevocable for its purpose, non-terminable at will, and extends to Clear Capital affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf. Do not double-flag ownership issues already raised under IP.

No audit heading appears. Rule targets audits of Clear Capital's usage or records; check Section 3 for a right to inspect our books in connection with compensation and Section 4 for any inspection of deliverable use. Audit rights we hold over Contractor's time and expense records benefit us and should not be flagged.

Directional rule. Look in Section 3 for late-payment penalties, kill fees or early-termination charges payable by Clear Capital, and in Section 7 for stipulated-damages language. Credits or damages running to us are acceptable and should not be flagged.

Section 5 pairs Contractor's representations and warranties with a warranty disclaimer — the disclaimer may gut the performance warranty. Check for a services warranty measured against the Specifications, a meaningful duration, and a real remedy (re-performance or refund) rather than an as-is disclaimer.

No insurance heading in the outline. If present it would most likely be appended to Section 5 (Contractor's representations) or Section 7 alongside liability and indemnity. Given Contractor performs Services and may touch our data, expect to raise this as missing if no coverage obligation is found.

Check Section 3 for guaranteed minimum fees, retainers or committed hours that Clear Capital must pay regardless of Services delivered, and Section 1 for any committed scope. A pure time-and-materials or milestone fee structure is not a take-or-pay and should not be flagged.

Section 6 (Termination) is the natural home for wind-down, return of materials and transition assistance; Section 4 may cover delivery of work product on termination. If neither addresses return of Clear Capital data and materials or continued assistance, treat as missing.
